# P7.3.1 findings after GUI experiment

## Observed identity behavior

| Experiment | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline | Imported successfully as `pla_test`; existing preset was replaced/selected. |
| Name only | Imported successfully as a new preset named `P7TEST_NAME_ONLY`. |
| Name + `filament_settings_id` | Imported successfully as a new preset named `P7TEST_NAME_SETTINGS_ID`. |
| Name with `inherits` preserved | Imported successfully as a new preset named `P7TEST_NAME_INHERITS`. |

The experiment demonstrates that `name` alone controls the visible custom
preset identity for this real GUI export. `inherits` remains
`Generic PLA @System`. No `setting_id` or `filament_id` was present in the
source, so their behavior remains untested.

## Evidence-based Worker rule

For this artifact shape, Orca canonicalization mutates only:

```text
name = {pi_code} @{printer}
pm_method_version = selected company method version
```

`filament_settings_id`, `inherits`, compatibility, version, and all material
parameters are preserved. This is the minimum mutation supported by the GUI
experiment.

## Remaining validation

`worker_canonical_candidate.json` was generated by the Orca processor using
context `PI=L2002CF`, `printer=BBL P2S`, `pm_method_version=2.1`. It imported
successfully with the expected name and parameters. The Orca re-export removed
`pm_method_version` while preserving all other compared fields. This
compatibility limitation is accepted by the business decision, so the final
production-readiness classification is `VALIDATED_WITH_LIMITATIONS`.
